assets.defect_engineered: barn reverb sits on the sibilants rather than as broadband noise; cleanup lifts intelligibility but leaves the tail of each cue ringing, and the ring is audible only when the cues are heard as a continuous run rather than one at a time
assets.content:
duration_s: 138 | roughen: true | script (verbatim, Dean Marchetti, one sitting in the barn): "Alright. Six movements, cues only, straight through.

Deadlift. Set the bar over the middle of the foot. Grip just outside the knees. Drop the hips, chest up, flatten the back. Take the slack out of the bar before you pull. Brace hard against the belt. Push the floor away and keep the bar close to the shins. Stand tall, lock the hips, don't lean back. Send it back down the way it came up, hinge first.

Back squat. Bar sits on the shelf of the back, not the neck. Brace first, then unrack and step back small. Break at the hips and the knees together. Sit down between your feet to depth. Drive the floor away and stand tall.

Overhead press. Bar in the heel of the hand, elbows just under it. Squeeze the glutes and brace the trunk. Press straight up and move the head back through. Finish with the bar stacked over the mid-foot.

Bench press. Eyes under the bar, shoulder blades pinched down and back. Feet flat, drive them into the floor. Unrack to over the shoulders. Lower with control to the lower chest. Elbows tucked to about forty-five. Touch, then press back and slightly toward the face. Lock out over the shoulders, not the throat.

Barbell row. Hinge to about parallel with a flat back. Let the bar hang under the shoulders. Pull the elbows past the ribs. Bring the bar to the lower ribs, not the chest. Squeeze the mid-back at the top. Lower it under control, don't drop it.

Front squat. Bar high on the front of the shoulders. Elbows up, upper arms parallel to the floor. Light fingertip grip, keep the rack solid. Brace the trunk hard. Big breath, break at the knees first. Keep the elbows up as you go down. Sit to depth with the chest tall. Drive up and the elbows stay high the whole way. Stand tall and reset the breath.

That's the six." | note: sibilant-dense cue tails (set, slack, shins, shelf, squeeze, shoulders, sits, chest, straight, stacked) ring into the following cue in the reverberant barn; gaps between cues are short so the ring overlaps the next cue's onset

assets.defect_engineered: the cue-list block is a single fixed-height text frame with auto-size OFF and no threaded overflow; it was drawn to the exact depth of last year's longest (six-cue) movement, so a record whose cue list runs longer renders to the frame's bottom edge and stops mid-line with no overset marker, while the merge reports success and the six-page count still equals the six-record count
assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the printer's existing Anvil and Oak exercise-card press PDF (flat, single record; to be reverse-engineered into a live six-record merge downstream).

Document: single portrait card, 127 x 178 mm (5 x 7 in) trim, 3 mm bleed present on all four sides (media box = trim + 3 mm), fonts embedded. This is the file the printer ran last year's six-card strip from.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (four apparent blocks, top to bottom):
- Top ~46 percent: a rectangular PICTURE BOX bleeding to the top and side card edges, holding the movement's poster frame.
- Below it: the MOVEMENT NAME in a heavy slightly-condensed slab display face, large, Anvil Iron.
- Under the name: a MUSCLE GROUP line in a plain humanist sans, small, Steel Grey.
- Lower two-thirds: a CUE LIST, a numbered list of coaching cues in the humanist sans, Anvil Iron with Oak numerals.
- Bottom-left corner: a small lockup of the recovered wordmark and the certification seal.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The PICTURE BOX is a genuine rectangular graphic frame, so a per-record poster frame can be bound into it through the merge's per-row image column - this part maps cleanly and is the frame the poster frame binds to.
- The MOVEMENT NAME and the MUSCLE GROUP line are two separate short text frames.
- The CUE LIST is a single FIXED-HEIGHT text frame: auto-size is OFF, there is no threaded second frame, and there is no visible overset indicator. Its height was set to the exact rendered depth of last year's longest cue list (six cues at last year's size and leading). A record whose cue list runs longer than six cues renders down to the frame's bottom edge and simply STOPS - mid-line, no ellipsis, no mark - and InDesign's merge still reports success and still emits exactly one page per record.
- So page count equal to record count is necessary but not sufficient: completeness of each cue list has to be confirmed on the rendered page.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content in the story text, not visible tokens): MOVEMENT_NAME | MUSCLE_GROUP | CUE_LIST | POSTER_FRAME

Colours: Chalk #F4F2ED ground, Anvil Iron #2B2B2E movement name and cue text, Steel Grey #8A9099 muscle-group line, Oak #6B4A2E cue numerals, Ember Rust #A6552F thin rule between the name and the cue block.
